svg.title: Cost curves, their lower envelope, and the constant
svg.text: 4. The answer: the maximum of the lower envelope, at a two-witness crossover
Each witness costs g(w,n) = |w|·sin²(θ_w/2) — LENGTH-WEIGHTED. The best witness at each α is the lower envelope (black); the
worst α is where that envelope peaks. It peaks at a kink, where the short misaligned (1,0) and the long well-aligned (2,1) cost the
same. Ignoring the length weight and simply taking the nearest direction gives 0.029909 — 1.56× too pessimistic (purple).
By the 8-fold lattice symmetry the octant [0°,45°] is the whole story; ε* = (3 − √5 − √(2√5 − 4))/4, a degree-4 algebraic number.
